newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries rally as inflation threat seems dim.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries rally as inflation threat seems dim.

text.p: Optimism that inflation remains contained drove the prices of U.S. Treasury securities higher on Friday as investors seemed none too concerned about next week's full slate of data.

The June Producer Price Index came in tame -- indicating there still was no inflationary pressure in the pipeline on the wholesale level. That news drove yields on the long bond as low as 6.51 percent, approaching the lowest level since December 10 when the bond closed at 6.49 percent. Some economists expect that level to be breached next week.
"We had an interesting series of events this morning and PPI really had no effect (on prices)," said Michael Strauss, chief economist at Sanwa Securities (USA) Co.
Strauss said that although the press would report Friday's activity was a result of PPI, two other factors moved the markets.
"There was some early forced selling by a variety of central banks after the Philipines devalued their currency -- they needed to reliquify themselves," Strauss said.
Then, in the afternoon, a tidal wave of buying came from holders of mortgage-backed securities and corporates.

"This came about due to concern over prepayment risk. As long as yields on the 10-year hover in the 6.20 percent range there will be buying (by holders of mortgage and corporate paper)," Strauss said.
"The market basically maintained a good tone. There's nothing to get in the way as long as inflation stays subdued," said Josh Feinman, vice president and global markets economist at Bankers Trust.
Feinman said "it's a brave new world" and he saw no roadblocks in the near term to disrupt the current economic environment.
In late trading, the 30-year bond was up 14/32 at 101-7/32 to yield 6.53 percent.

The two-year note was unchanged at 100-6/32 to yield 5.90 percent. The five-year note was up 3/32 at 100-17/32 with a yield of 6.12 percent. The 10-year note closed 6/32 higher at 102-28/32 to yield 6.23 percent.
The three-month bill was down four basis points to 4.99 percent. The six-month bill was unchanged at 5.10 percent and the year-bill was down one basis point at 5.22 percent.
